subject: Clarifying customer output ownership, training opt-outs and telemetry/feedback license
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-systems.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@atlas-systems.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarifying output ownership + training opt-outs

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal reviewed the MSA/order form and flagged two areas we need clearer language on before procurement signs: (1) customer ownership of generated output, and (2) the ability to opt out of model training using our content.

High level asks from Atlas:
- Explicit statement that Atlas owns all customer-provided input and all generated output produced by the service when using their account and configuration.
- A concrete opt-out mechanism so Atlas data is never used to further train or fine-tune Redwood or third-party models.
- A telemetry/feedback clause: Atlas is OK with anonymized usage telemetry for performance/ops, but not any retention that could be used to reconstruct customer content.

They attached a redline of the MSA (Atlas_MSA_redline_20270629.docx). Can you run this by legal and product to confirm what we can accept and propose alternative wording where necessary? We need a response by EOD Friday so procurement can proceed.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Director of ML Platforms | Atlas Systems

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-systems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, k arthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarifying output ownership + training opt-outs

Alex —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Solutions) to propose language and confirm operational controls. Quick confirmations from my side before Legal weighs in:

1) Ownership of output: Our standard position is to grant customers ownership of "Customer Output" (defined as content generated from the customer's input) subject to any third-party model license terms for upstream model weights. We can commit to a statement in the MSA that avoids us assigning ownership of the base model or any general model improvements.

2) Training opt-out: We do offer a training/data opt-out for Enterprise contracts. We need to define the scope (raw input, generated output, and metadata). Operationally, opt-out requires a per-tenant flag and prevents data from entering any training pipelines and from being retained beyond operational windows. There may be a 24–72 hour window for short-term logs used for debugging unless Atlas requests immediate deletion; we can discuss stricter retention.

3) Telemetry & feedback: We typically collect aggregated and anonymized telemetry for reliability and to improve serving efficiency. We can add a carveout: no retention of content fields and only aggregated metrics.

Laura/Karthik — can you propose redline text that addresses Atlas's language and indicates where we need to push back? I sketched a first pass below (please refine):

PROPOSED (draft — needs Legal):
"Customer Output. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Output (defined as text, files or other content generated by the Service in response to Customer Data). Redwood retains ownership of its platform, models (including underlying weights), and any general improvements that are not derived solely from Customer Data.

Training. Except to the extent expressly permitted in a Customer-specific opt-in, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's models or third-party models. Customer may elect to opt out of such use by notifying Redwood in writing, and Redwood will implement an account-level opt-out within a commercially reasonable timeframe.

Telemetry and Feedback. Redwood may collect telemetry and feedback limited to aggregated, non-content telemetry for operational performance, capacity planning, and system monitoring. Redwood will not retain raw content fields or data that could be used to reconstruct Customer Data or Customer Output."

If that looks OK, I will have Legal produce a redline and we can send back.

- Soojin
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, k arthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Clarifying output ownership + training opt-outs

So —

Thanks for the summary, Soojin. I reviewed Atlas's redline and sketched responses inline in the attached doc. Key positions and compromise language below: 

1) Ownership: We will accept a clause clarifying customer ownership of Customer Output, but we need an explicit carveout preserving Redwood's rights in platform code, tooling, model weights, and any derivative improvements that are abstract and cannot be traced to a specific customer's data. Suggested sentence: 
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall retain all right, title and interest in the Service, platform tooling, model weights, and generalized improvements that are not uniquely derived from Customer Data."

2) Training opt-out: We can provide an opt-out that covers Customer Data and Customer Output. Operational notes: opt-out will prevent data from entering any training pipelines and will disable export to any internal sandbox used for model development. However, we cannot retroactively expunge data used prior to opt-out; we will commit to not using data after the opt-out effective date. Proposed redline language: 
"Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train, fine-tune, or improve any models after the effective date of Customer's opt-out election. Data processed prior to such election may have been used in internal improvement workflows and cannot be retroactively removed from prior model snapshot artifacts."

3) Telemetry/Feedback: We'll accept limited telemetry but need to preserve ability to collect operational logs for security and reliability. Compromise language: 
"Redwood may collect and retain anonymized operational telemetry (e.g., latency, error rates, aggregated token counts). Redwood will not retain raw content fields or data that could be reasonably reconstructed into Customer Data. For debugging high-severity incidents, Redwood may retain request-level logs for up to 14 days and will provide Atlas with the option to request a secure review or redaction of such logs."

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm runbooks/ops controls for the 14-day debug retention and the tenant-level opt-out flag so we can give Atlas concrete timelines? I'll produce a formal redline to send back once we have the operational notes.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: k arthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-systems.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Clarifying output ownership + training opt-outs

Laura / Soojin —

Operational confirmation below so Legal can close the language and we can push back on overly broad Atlas asks: 

- Tenant opt-out flag: We have an account-level opt-out feature in our Enterprise admin console. Activating opt-out immediately routes all future telemetry and content through an internal pipeline that blocks export to any training queues. Implementation ETA: immediate for existing Enterprise customers with a manual toggle (we'll implement an API toggle within 5 business days if Atlas needs automation).

- Retention windows: We retain request-level logs in a hot store for 14 days (used for debugging, traces). After 14 days request-level logs are moved to a short-term bucket for an additional 16 days for compliance, unless the customer requests earlier deletion. For opt-out accounts we will implement accelerated purge for model training pipelines within 48 hours of the opt-out flag; the 14-day debugging window still applies unless Atlas requests an exemption and acceptable proof of data removal steps is documented.

- No model retraining: Once opt-out is enabled, the tenant's data and outputs will be excluded from any retraining or fine-tuning jobs. We cannot guarantee removal from previously trained snapshots.

I also attached a short spreadsheet (Training_OptOut_Table.xlsx) mapping customer-visible options to backend controls and who owns each step (Ops, Prod, Legal).

If that aligns, Laura — feel free to finalize the redline and I'll confirm the specific runbook steps (who runs the purge, audit log entries, and timeline).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-systems.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, k arthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarifying output ownership + training opt-outs

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal at Atlas: 

- Atlas will accept a 14-day debug retention period if Redwood commits to providing an audit report on request and a secure redaction path. Can you include a line in the MSA that commits to an audit response timeline (e.g., 7 business days) for requests related to retention and redaction?

- Can we make the opt-out effective immediately from Redwood's side (Atlas will trigger it via the account toggle) and have Redwood provide a confirmation email once the backend blocking is in place?

- Final ask: include a short "scope" example in the order form that shows explicitly that prompts, attachments, and model outputs are covered by the opt-out. Atlas procurement wants that explicit list in the order form to avoid ambiguity.

If Redwood can accept those three items, Atlas is prepared to move to signatures and DocuSign.

Alex
Director of ML Platforms | Atlas Systems
